As of 540 AM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Sunny and dry Fall weather continues.

High pressure remains centered north of the local area, centered 
over interior portions of New England and SE Canada. Meanwhile, a 
coastal low lingers well offshore. Temps as of 540 AM ranged 
from the mid to upper 40s for most inland areas and upper 50s 
to around 60 along the coast. The low has consistently been 
farther east than models indicated over the past few days. As 
such, it is difficult to believe that the low will nudge back 
west at this point into high pressure. Nevertheless, models 
still try to show the low nudging a bit west today while 
deepening. Given the uncertainty, have kept the outer cloud 
shield from the low reaching far eastern portions of the area 
later this afternoon into this evening before clouds move back 
over the ocean as the low pulls away tonight. However, even this
may be overdone and it is entirely possible that only a portion
of the Eastern Shore sees any clouds today with the vast 
majority of the forecast area likely remaining sunny. Given the 
trend for sunny conditions today, temps have trended warmer with
highs in the mid 60s across the coast as well as the Eastern 
Shore and upper 60s elsewhere. Temps may even reach 70F in a few
locations.

The coastal low moves farther offshore Thu with high pressure 
gradually building south into the region through the weekend. This 
will allow for stagnant weather pattern with sunny and dry weather 
continuing for the foreseeable future. In fact, some model guidance 
shows completely dry conditions through the end of the month. 
Temperatures remain seasonable Thu with highs in the upper 60s to 
around 70F. However, as the cool, strong high builds into the region 
Fri into the weekend, cooler temperatures arrive with highs in the 
lower 60s for most Fri and Sat (potentially upper 50s across the 
Eastern Shore and mid 60s across NE NC). Temperatures moderate back 
into the mid-upper 60s by Sun and upper 60s to lower 70s Mon and 
Tue. Meanwhile, lows are expected to range from the upper 30s across 
the Piedmont and typically cooler locations near I-95 to the lower 
40s east of I-95 and around 50F along the coast tonight into Thu 
morning. As such, some patchy frost is possible across mainly the 
Piedmont. However, temperatures don't look to be cool enough to 
support Frost Advisories at this time. The better chance for a more 
widespread frost is Fri night into Sat morning with the high 
centered just to the north of the local area. The best chance for 
frost will once again be across the Piedmont and typically cooler 
interior portions of the Northern Neck and S/SE VA. Currently have 
lows that night in the mid-upper 30s across the Piedmont, upper 30s 
for most inland areas far from the coast, 40s closer to the coast, 
and lower 50s along the coast. However, given the strength of the 
high, it is possible that Louisa gets down to around 32-33F. As such 
will have to monitor trends in case Frost Advisories are warranted. 
Sat night/Sun morning will also be cool with additional patchy frost 
possible, however, it will likely not be as cool as Fri night/Sat 
morning. Otherwise, winds remain breezy mainly along the coast each 
day through Fri with gusts up to 25-30 mph today and 20-25 mph Thu 
an Fri. Inland will not be as breezy, however, gusts up to 20-25 mph 
are possible today with occasional gusts up to around 20 mph 
possible Thu and Fri.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Prolonged onshore flow will lead to multiple 
elevated tide cycles this week resulting in rounds of coastal 
flooding.

The ETSS, PETSS and STOFS continue to suggest the anomalies will 
continue to increase today with 2-3 ft anomalies expected. This
may allow some of the sites more prone to flooding (Lynnhaven, 
Smithfield, Bayford, etc.) to touch moderate flooding during the
high tides later this afternoon/evening and potentially again
Thursday AM. The only location with enough confidence for a
warning is Lynnhaven, mainly due to the very large swell at the
mouth of the Chesapeake Bay likely aiding in the flood
potential. Models have trended too high for this entire event 
so far and the confidence is just not there to issue any 
additional warnings at this time. Otherwise, extended the 
Coastal Flood Advisories out another high tide cycle and now 
have most of them running through locations adjacent to the 
York and Rappahannock Rivers. 

The low finally starts to move northeast by Thursday, which 
should allow for the winds to subside and also the water levels,
except for the upper bay where water levels likely rise as some
water gets trapped in the bay in response to stronger flood 
tides at the mouth of the bay owing to the weaker winds. Coastal
Flood Advisories were issued for our Maryland Eastern Shore
locations to account for this. In addition, Bishops Head and
Tangier Island may both approach or exceed moderate flood stage,
with the best potential during the Thursday AM high
